title: Scrape a bee stinger out with a bank card's edge
instruction: Get the bee stinger out of the back of the hand with the bank card standing in the block, then lay the card down on the table and let go. Only the card may touch the stinger.
context: Why: a honeybee leaves its stinger in the skin with the venom sac still attached, and getting it out is everyday first aid most people have done or watched, on themselves or a child. MedlinePlus (Insect bites and stings) says to remove it by scraping the back of a credit card or other straight-edged object across it, and not to use tweezers, which may squeeze the venom sac and release more venom; the NHS says to scrape it sideways with a fingernail or the edge of a bank card. So the familiar move, pinching it out, is the wrong one: the job is not a grasp at all but an edge drawn sideways along soft skin. The hard part is physical: holding a 0.76 mm card by one long edge and running the other edge across the skin low enough to catch a 3 mm stub at its base, pressing lightly enough not to dig in or push the stub down, so that it tips over and slides out of its track. Done by: parents and carers, school nurses, first-aiders, gardeners and beekeepers.
setup: Positions are centres in cm from the arm bases' midpoint: x forward, y left; heights above the table. Pine block: 15 x 15 x 2 cm, screwed to the table at x 32, y -6. Hand: a pose-able left female silicone mannequin hand, life size (sold as a display prop, about US$65), about 21 x 11.4 x 6.4 cm and 0.5 kg, skin-tone platinum silicone over a wire armature, lying palm down on the block, fingers pointing at the robot, held by two hook-and-loop straps (across the palm and the wrist). The back of the hand is level along the middle finger's knuckle bone; the sting site is there, at x 31, y -6, 5.5 cm above the table, marked by a 12 mm black ink ring drawn round it. Stinger: a stand-in, a 6 mm piece of black 0.5 mm nylon monofilament (fishing line) with a 1.5 mm bead of black UV-cured resin on its outer end (the venom sac) and a thin white paint ring 2 mm above where it enters the skin, about 3 minutes to make and cure. It sits upright in a track first made with a 0.5 mm needle at the ring's centre, 3 mm in and 3 mm standing out (bead included). Card: a blank white PVC card, CR80 bank-card size, 85.6 x 54 x 0.76 mm, 5.5 g, standing on its long edge in a 1 mm saw kerf 10 mm deep along the top of a pine block (8 x 3 x 2 cm, taped down at x 24, y -22, long side along x), 44 mm of it standing out. Cameras: the station's top camera, and a side camera (1080p, phone telephoto) on a tripod beyond the table's far edge, lens at x 70, y -6, level with the back of the hand, looking back toward the robot along the middle finger's line, so the scrape (along y) is seen side-on; nothing stands on the hand. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored from the side video (level with the back of the hand, looking along the hand, so the scrape is seen side-on) and the top video; a 5x magnifier after the trial. Drawn: how far the stinger has slid out along its track, from its 3 mm in at the start. Out: drawn 3 mm, no part of it left in the track (it lies loose or has come off the skin; magnifier). Tipped: its lean from upright, read on the side video frame with an on-screen protractor against the skin's line. Highest rung reached, read at the end: 0: none of the below. 0.25: the card has tipped the stinger 30 degrees or more at any moment (side video). 0.5: the stinger is out. 0.75: also the card lies flat on the table (its highest corner under 5 mm; not on the hand or either block) and no gripper touches it. 1.0: also both grippers at least 30 mm from the hand and card, the hand moved no more than 5 mm in the trial (top video against the block's edge), and everything still for 1 s. 0 whatever else happens, even if later undone: a gripper finger touches the stinger (seen touching it on either video, or the stinger moving with a finger on it); the stinger is pushed 2 mm or more further into its track (its white ring, 2 mm above the skin at the start, is in the skin on a side-video frame where nothing touches the stinger: pressed down on the sac; a tipped stinger keeps its ring in view); the hand comes off its block (moves 2 cm or tips 10 degrees). The sim reads the same: drawn is the stinger's slide along its track, out is 3 mm drawn, and a gripper finger touches it at contact (0.02 mm).
reset_notes: A fresh stinger stand-in each trial, pushed into the same track at the ring's centre, upright (a square held beside it) until its white ring sits 2 mm above the skin. Check it with a 0 to 2 N push-pull gauge on the bead: along its line it must not slide out under 0.3 N and must slide out under 1 N; pushed sideways it must tip 30 degrees between 0.3 and 1.5 N and stand back up. A new track (every ~10 trials, 5 mm along the knuckle bone, with the ink ring moved) is accepted once one scrape by hand with the card takes a stand-in out. Stand the card back in its kerf, long edge down. Strap the hand back on its tape marks. Run with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Approximate. The hand is stacked boxes, 0.5 kg, loose on the block (strapped in reality); the scrape is on its flat back, a 4 mm skin pad that dents at 1 N per mm. The stinger, drawn 0.5 mm with its bead, collides as a 1.5 mm square stick 3 mm out, leaning on two hinges at the skin (0.003 N m/rad) and sliding along its track against 0.5 N; once out it stays on its line, up to 8 mm out. The card is a 0.76 mm box.
scores: Dream-1 run: refused at step 32; demo: 1.0
